name: Rhinovirus (common cold)
short_description: Tiny non-enveloped icosahedral +ssRNA virus (~30 nm) of the Picornaviridae (genus Enterovirus, species Rhinovirus A/B/C) whose ~170 genotypes cause most common colds; it replicates best at the cool 33-35 °C of the nasal lining and docks onto ICAM-1 through a canyon-shaped groove in its capsid.

textbook.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — muted dusty educational palette on dark charcoal, thin clean outlines, correctly NAKED capsid (no envelope, no spikes): raised star-shaped VP1 mesas at the five-fold vertices, olive canyon grooves ringing each mesa, teal VP2 / rose VP3 propeller facets, and a quarter cut-away showing the pale sage VP4 lining, ONE continuous coppery ssRNA thread with a single indigo VPg bead and the ochre pocket factor. No text, no border, no face. Chosen as label base.

sem.1: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — photorealistic false-colour SEM of a single naked icosahedral virion on a slate-teal substrate: bare protein surface with no spikes or fringe, star-shaped five-fold plateaus and clearly sunken canyon grooves, warm sand-amber body with olive shadows, fills the frame edge-to-edge, surface only (no internals), no text/border.

3d.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-3-pro-image) — natural biological tints and correct naked-capsid relief, but TWO indigo beads were drawn instead of one VPg, the ochre pocket factor floated free in the hollow instead of sitting inside the capsid wall, and the shell read as separate tiles stuck onto a ball rather than an interlocking mosaic.
3d.2: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — fixed: exactly one VPg bead on one end of a single irregular coppery RNA thread, the pocket factor now embedded in the cut edge of a VP1 wedge, and the shell reads as one continuous interlocking mosaic of amber VP1 mesas, olive canyon depressions and teal/rose VP2-VP3 facets over a pale sage VP4 lining. Natural tints, dark studio background, no text/border/face.

watercolor.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL (gemini-3-pro-image) — full-bleed aged paper was correct, but the five-fold plateaus were painted as flat decorative cartoon stars on coin-like medallions instead of raised faceted protein mounds, and the genome was drawn as a regular coil spring rather than a loosely coiled thread.
watercolor.2: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — warm aged paper fills the frame corner-to-corner with a soft dark wash halo (no sheet, mat or frame); the mesas are now shaded three-dimensional faceted domes sunk in olive canyon rings, VP2/VP3 form convincing three-fold propellers, and the cut-away shows the sage VP4 lining, one irregular coppery ssRNA thread with a single indigo VPg bead and the ochre pocket factor. No text, no border.

reference: ✅ PASS (with a provenance caveat) — no properly-licensed conventional TEM/SEM plate of a rhinovirus virion exists in CDC PHIL, the NIAID Flickr stream or Wikimedia Commons (Commons carries only X-ray-derived renderings), so the reference is the wwPDB EMDB entry image for EMD-12171, a genuine cryo-electron-microscopy reconstruction of a native human rhinovirus 14 particle (Hrebik et al. 2021, PNAS), CC0. It shows exactly what the science section describes: a single naked icosahedral capsid with radially false-coloured relief — yellow star-shaped mesas at the five-fold vertices, blue canyon depressions ringing them and green propeller facets between — and no envelope or spikes. Cleaned with edit_image.py (dark uniform background, sharpened, colorization and shape preserved).
decision: gemini-3-pro-image; cleanest separation of structures for labelling
